title: Æbleflæsk (fried pork belly with apples and thyme)

ingredients.name: salted or streaky pork belly, cut into small cubes

steps: Fry the pork cubes in a large dry pan over medium heat for 10 to 12 minutes until they release their fat and turn golden.
Add the onion and cook for 3 minutes.
Stir in the apples, sugar, thyme and water.
Cover and simmer gently for 10 to 15 minutes until the apples are soft and the mixture has thickened.
Serve warm or cold on dark rye bread.

title: Bøfsandwich (Danish beef patty sandwich with remoulade and crispy onions)

ingredients.name: soft rolls or white bread buns

steps: Mix the beef with the egg, salt and pepper until just combined and shape into four flat patties.
Heat the oil in a frying pan over medium-high heat and cook the patties for 4 to 5 minutes per side until browned and cooked through.
Split and lightly toast the rolls.
Spread the remoulade on both sides, then layer on the patty, pickle slices, ketchup and mustard.
Top with crispy onions and serve warm.

title: Brændende kærlighed (burning love: mash with bacon and onions)
steps: Boil the potatoes in salted water for 20 minutes until tender, drain and mash with the butter and warm milk until smooth.
Season with nutmeg, salt and pepper and keep warm.
Fry the bacon in a dry pan for 5 minutes until crisp, then lift it out, leaving the fat behind.
Cook the onions in the bacon fat for 10 minutes until soft and golden.
Pile the mash onto plates, make a well in the middle and top with the bacon and onions with their fat.
Serve with pickled beetroot on the side.

title: Flæskesteg (Danish roast pork with crackling)

ingredients.name: pork loin or shoulder roast with the rind on

steps: Heat the oven to 180 degrees C. Score the rind in thin parallel lines about 1 cm apart, taking care not to cut into the meat.
Rub the salt into the rind and the pepper over the meat, then tuck the bay leaves into the cuts.
Place the roast rind side up in a roasting tin and pour the water into the tin, not over the meat.
Roast for about 1 hour 30 minutes until the internal temperature reaches 70 degrees C.
Raise the oven to 250 degrees C, or use the grill, and roast for another 10 to 15 minutes until the rind blisters and turns crisp, watching it closely.
Rest the meat for 15 minutes. Meanwhile pour the pan juices into a saucepan, whisk in the flour, then the cream, and simmer to make the gravy.
Slice and serve with the gravy, potatoes and red cabbage.

title: Jødekager (Danish cinnamon-sugar butter cookies)
steps: Rub the butter into the flour and sugar until crumbly, then mix in the yolk to form a dough. Chill for 30 minutes.
Heat the oven to 190 degrees C. Roll the dough to 3 mm thick and cut into rounds about 5 cm across.
Place the rounds on a lined tray and brush with beaten egg.
Mix the topping sugar, cinnamon and almonds and sprinkle over each cookie.
Bake for 8 to 10 minutes until pale golden at the edges. Cool on a rack.

title: Klenät (twisted fried pastry knots)
steps: Rub the cold butter into the flour and sugar until crumbly.
Add the egg yolks and lemon juice and knead briefly into a firm dough. Wrap and chill for 1 hour.
Roll the dough out to about 4 mm thick and cut into strips about 3 cm wide and 8 cm long.
Make a lengthwise slit in the middle of each strip and pull one end through the slit to form a knot.
Heat the oil to 170 degrees C and fry the knots in batches for 2 to 3 minutes, turning once, until golden.
Drain on paper towels and dust with icing sugar once cool.

title: Koldskål (chilled buttermilk soup with vanilla and lemon)
steps: Stir the buttermilk, sugar, vanilla and lemon zest together in a large bowl until the sugar is dissolved.
Chill for at least 1 hour so that the flavours blend.
Pour into bowls and add sliced strawberries.
Serve very cold with the biscuits crumbled on top or served alongside.

title: Kransekage (almond ring cake tower)
steps: Heat the oven to 180 degrees C and grease six ring-shaped tins or line a tray with baking paper.
Mix the ground almonds and icing sugar and add enough egg white to bring them to a stiff marzipan-like dough. Chill for 30 minutes.
Roll the dough into ropes about 1 cm thick and fit them into rings of graduated sizes, joining the ends.
Bake for 12 to 15 minutes until pale golden and slightly firm. Cool completely.
Mix the egg white, icing sugar and lemon juice into a thick icing and pipe zigzag lines over each ring.
Stack the rings, largest on the bottom, into a tower and serve in slices.

title: Millionbøf (Danish beef in tomato sauce)
steps: Heat the oil in a large pan and brown the beef over high heat, breaking it into small crumbs.
Add the onions and pepper and cook for 5 minutes until soft.
Stir in the flour, tomato paste and paprika and cook for 1 minute.
Add the crushed tomatoes and stock and simmer for 25 minutes, stirring occasionally, until thick.
Season to taste and serve over mashed potatoes, rice or pasta.

title: Risalamande (Danish rice pudding with whipped cream and cherry sauce)
steps: Simmer the rice with the milk, vanilla pod and sugar over low heat for 35 to 40 minutes, stirring now and then, until thick and creamy.
Remove the vanilla pod and cool the rice completely in the fridge.
Whip the cream to soft peaks and fold it into the cold rice along with the chopped almonds.
For the sauce, heat the cherries and their juice with the sugar, stir in the cornflour mixed with a little cold water and simmer for 2 minutes until glossy.
Serve the pudding in bowls with the warm or cooled cherry sauce spooned over.

title: Rødgrød med fløde (Danish red berry pudding with cream)
steps: Put the berries, water and sugar in a saucepan and bring to a simmer. Cook for 10 minutes until the fruit is soft.
Stir the starch with a little cold water to make a smooth paste.
Pour the paste slowly into the simmering fruit, stirring constantly, and cook for a minute or two until thick and glossy.
Pour into a serving bowl and cool, sprinkling a little sugar on top to stop a skin forming.
Chill until cold and serve with cold cream poured over.

title: Stegt flæsk med persillesovs (fried pork belly with parsley sauce)

ingredients.name: pork belly, sliced about 5 mm thick

steps: Peel the potatoes and boil them in salted water for 20 minutes until tender.
Meanwhile heat a large dry frying pan over medium heat and lay in the pork slices without overlapping, working in batches.
Fry for 5 to 6 minutes per side until deep golden and crisp, seasoning with salt and pepper. Keep warm in a low oven.
For the sauce, melt the butter, stir in the flour and cook for 1 minute, then whisk in the milk and simmer for 5 minutes until thick.
Stir in the parsley and season to taste.
Serve the crisp pork with the potatoes and plenty of parsley sauce.

title: Tebirkes (poppy seed pastry with remonce)
steps: Mix the flour, yeast, sugar and salt, then add the milk and egg and knead into a smooth dough. Chill for 30 minutes.

Roll out the dough into a rectangle and place the cold butter, flattened between baking paper into a slab, on two-thirds of it. Fold into a letter fold, turn and roll out again, then fold again. Chill for 30 minutes.
Beat together the remonce: the soft butter, sugar and grated marzipan.
Roll the dough out thinly, spread with the remonce and cut into 8 squares or triangles.
Fold each piece in half to enclose the filling, place on a lined tray and let rise for 40 minutes.
Heat the oven to 200 degrees C. Brush with beaten egg and sprinkle generously with poppy seeds.
Bake for 15 to 18 minutes until golden and puffed.
